SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Acute onset shortness of breath while sitting, began ≈1 hour ago.
- Associated symptoms: Dry cough since yesterday; palpitations (“heart really going”); chest feels sore on deep inspiration; C-section scar tenderness.
- Negative symptoms: No chest pain at rest; no sputum production; no baby cough/cold symptoms.
- Obstetric history: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- Past medical history: No chronic conditions reported other than recent C-section.
- Medications:
  • Codeine – dose/route/frequency not documented; taken regularly post-op but none for ~1 week.
- Allergies:
  • Ibuprofen – reaction not specified.
- Social history: Lives with partner (currently at work); caring for 4-week-old infant at home; able to self-transport to hospital.

Objective:
- Vital signs: Not formally measured. Self-counted radial pulse: 30 beats over clinician-timed interval (exact duration not documented). Clinician impression: heart rate “slightly fast.”
- No other examination findings documented.
- Investigations: None performed during call.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute shortness of breath postpartum
   - Assessment: Suspected pulmonary embolism.
   - Differential diagnosis: Anxiety/panic episode, postoperative atelectasis or pneumonia (dry cough), other cardiopulmonary causes.
   - Investigations planned: Evaluation in hospital (likely imaging and blood tests per ED protocol) – patient advised to attend immediately.
   - Treatment planned: Emergency department assessment; withhold further Codeine until evaluated.
   - Referrals: Emergency department; ambulance offered, patient opted for self-transport with infant.

2. Post-cesarean pain management
   - Assessment: Resolving postoperative pain; currently not taking analgesia for ~1 week.
   - Treatment planned: Temporarily avoid Codeine until after hospital evaluation; pain management to be revisited once acute issue addressed.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Full vital signs (BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature); detailed allergy reaction; complete medication list/reconciliation; obstetric/gynecologic history details; smoking status.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; no significant inaudible sections.
